title: Unify route manifests and decommission legacy flag transport
creator: Samir Patel
description:
Summary:
We will collapse multiple versioned routing/config surfaces (route-manifests v0/v1 legacy variants, legacy flag transport endpoints, and the old rollout redirect paths) into a single canonical manifest that the runtime and Console will read. This ticket removes the legacy flag transport pipeline (the /api/v0/flags push and the DB-backed compat layer that rewrote routing keys), migrates active rollouts to the canonical manifest format, and retires the compatibility HTTP endpoints and redirect logic.

Motivation:
- Legacy transport and multiple manifest versions add runtime branching, increase CPU/alloc costs, and complicate kernel selection and caching.
- Consolidating into a single manifest simplifies rollouts, reduces on-path checks, and eliminates a thin-but-wide class of bugs observed in long-tail rollouts.

Scope & Goals:
1) Implement a canonical route manifest schema and a migration tool to convert active manifests from v0/v1 -> canonical.
2) Stop writing to legacy flag transport endpoints and migrate producers to the new publish API.
3) Remove the compat HTTP endpoints (/api/v0/flags, /rollout-compat/*) and the path-based redirect middleware.
4) Update runtime routing to depend only on canonical manifests and delete the runtime branching code paths.
5) Run a safe rollout with feature gates, canarying, and automated rollback on errors.

Non-goals:
- This ticket does not change rollout semantics or evaluation logic; it only consolidates config surfaces.

High-level Plan:
A) Analysis & discovery (done): inventory of active manifests and clients that post to legacy endpoints. Produced a list of 142 distinct clients and 28 active rollouts still using compat transport.
B) Migration tooling (in progress): build a one-shot converter utility that reads legacy manifests and outputs canonical manifests, with validation and a dry-run mode.
C) Producer migration: update internal services (flag-service, rollout-service, infra-provisioner) to publish canonical manifests. Provide a short compatibility shim package for internal clients.
D) Runtime guarded switch: add a config flag runtime.use_canonical_manifests (default: false) and a rollout window to move traffic to the canonical path per-region.
E) Deprecation & removal: after 2 weeks of canaries and no regression, flip the flag global, remove compat code, and close the legacy endpoints.
F) Cleanup & audits: delete schema v0/v1 parsers, remove docs, and archive manifest migration logs.

Migration details:
- Data migration will be performed in-place with idempotent converters; every converted manifest will be written to the new manifests table and annotated with a migration checksum.
- A verification job will compare runtime resolution results between legacy and canonical parsing for a 48-hour dry-run window.
- For any rollout with active traffic > 5 RPS we will run manual P0 review and schedule a plateaued canary phase.

Tests & Validation:
- Unit tests for converter and schema validation (target 100% coverage on schema mapping).
- Integration tests with runtime in a staging cluster that replays a 72-hour snapshot of production routing traffic.
- Synthetic traffic tests to exercise cold-start, caching, and KV behavior under canonical manifests.

Monitoring & Rollback:
- Dashboards: manifest-coverage, parse-errors, routing-delta, latency-by-route. Links: https://dash.redwood.internal/d/manifest-coverage
- Alerting: page on > 1% parse-errors over 10m or routing-delta > 2% for a critical route.
- Rollback: re-enable legacy compat flag and redeploy runtime build that contains the compat code. We will maintain the compat branch for 30 days after the flip.

Risks & Mitigations:
- Risk: Some internal clients can't be migrated quickly. Mitigation: provide shim library (compat-client) and run short-term proxy while owners migrate.
- Risk: Unexpected routing deltas. Mitigation: staged canaries with automated traffic comparison and manual P0 path.

Deliverables:
- converter tool with dry-run and migration reports (artifact: s3://redwood-artifacts/manifest-converter/ENG-62345)
- updated producer SDKs and internal compat-client package
- runtime change behind runtime.use_canonical_manifests feature flag
- decommission plan and post-mortem template

Next steps (short term):
- Complete the converter unit and integration tests (owner: Lena Park, ETA: 2025-10-22).
- Begin producer migrations with two low-traffic services (flag-service and infra-provisioner) as first canaries (owner: Diego Morales).
- Schedule a canary window for eu-west-1 cluster for 2025-10-30.
